title: Manage ATM Service Slots
real_world_story: An ATM service system has a fixed number of request slots for temporarily storing customer requests. When requests are removed from the front, newly arriving requests should be able to reuse the freed slots.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Enqueue and dequeue operations on ATM requests
real_world_connection.target_represents: Requests currently stored in the fixed-size request buffer
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: A circular queue that reuses positions freed after dequeue operations

problem_statement: Implement a circular queue of capacity C that processes a sequence of enqueue and dequeue operations. For every dequeue operation, print the removed customer ID. If an enqueue is attempted when the queue is full, ignore that operation. If a dequeue is attempted when the queue is empty, ignore that operation.
task: Process all operations using a circular queue and print the customer IDs removed by valid dequeue operations.
input_format: The first line contains two integers C and Q, representing the queue capacity and number of operations. Each of the next Q lines contains either 'ENQUEUE X' or 'DEQUEUE'.
output_format: For every successful DEQUEUE operation, print the removed customer ID on a separate line. If no dequeue operation is successful, print -1.

examples.input:
3 7
ENQUEUE 101
ENQUEUE 202
ENQUEUE 303
DEQUEUE
ENQUEUE 404
DEQUEUE
DEQUEUE
examples.explanation: Customer 101 is removed first. Its slot is reused by customer 404, while the remaining customers continue to follow FIFO order.
The third enqueue is ignored because the queue is full. The first two customers are then removed in FIFO order.

expected_algorithm.name: Circular Queue Operations
expected_algorithm.reason: A circular queue allows freed positions at the beginning of a fixed-size queue to be reused efficiently.

hint: Move the rear position circularly when inserting an element.
Move the front position circularly when removing an element.
Track the current number of elements to identify full and empty states.
real_world_takeaway: Circular queues are useful for fixed-size ATM or banking request buffers because they reuse memory positions instead of shifting stored requests.
